clue.text: Bought furniture to hold kid

indicators.note: the furniture word is made to hold, that is contain, the word for kid

parts.note: a bed is an item of furniture
to kid someone is to tease or rib them

explanation.surface: Someone buys a piece of furniture big enough to hold a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child, but here it is the verb meaning to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: To bribe someone is to buy their favour or co-operation, so bribed is a sense of bought.

clue.text: Back up when pierced by Greek character's sword

indicators.note: the reversed word is pierced, that is has something stuck through it, by the Greek letter
in a down clue, up means the word for back is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the back of something is its rear
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A warrior backs away when stabbed by a Greek's sword.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'up' is a reversal signal, and 'pierced by' puts the Greek letter partway through the turned word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender, sharp-pointed thrusting sword.

clue.text: Musical instrument carried by idol in Birmingham

indicators.note: the words for carried by and idol are placed in the nickname for Birmingham

parts.note: Brum is the informal name for Birmingham, England's second city
something carried by a vehicle is on it
an idol is a god that is worshipped

explanation.surface: A pop idol in Birmingham is carrying an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: BRUM is the everyday nickname for Birmingham, the big city in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A bongo drum is a small hand drum played in pairs, a percussion instrument.

clue.text: One's yard's tidied for period of bright weather

indicators.note: tidied means the letters of these words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's garden gets tidied up during a spell of sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry season is the part of the year in some climates with little rain and plenty of sunshine.

clue.text: Poodle is going nuts near water

indicators.note: going nuts means going crazy, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A pet poodle goes wild beside a pond or pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Poolside describes somewhere beside a swimming pool, which is close to water.

clue.text: Waffle not turnover taken from London station

indicators.note: the reversed word is taken away from the station's name

parts.note: Paddington is a major railway terminus in London

indicators.note: turnover tells us to turn the word not over, reading it backwards

explanation.surface: Waffle about turnover at a London station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like business jargon but reverses NOT into TON, which comes off PADDINGTON, a big London railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: Padding is superfluous material added to fill out speech or writing, the same as waffle.

clue.text: Main residents of Windsor Castle

indicators.note: the residents are taken out of the letters of these words, which hold them inside

explanation.surface: Asks who chiefly lives at the royal home, Windsor Castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like 'chief', but it is the old poetic word for the sea; WINDSOR CASTLE is a royal residence in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Killer whales live in the oceans, and the main is a literary word for the sea.

clue.text: Second place containing oil to blow up

parts.note: an oil well is a place from which oil comes

explanation.surface: A second site holding oil is set to be blown up.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell is to expand or inflate, much as something blown up does.

clue.text: Dragging around two short jockeys

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre about, so these letters are shuffled
short means the word two loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Something drags on around two jockeys who are small.
explanation.walkthrough: Jockeys look like riders, but here the word is a verb meaning to manoeuvre, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dragging is drawn-out, going on for longer than it should.

clue.text: Aware of Cockney's ambition, yen to stop inadequacy

parts.note: a Cockney drops the h, so hope becomes 'ope

indicators.note: the yen symbol stops up, that is plugs, the word for inadequacy

parts.note: need is a lack or shortfall
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A Londoner's dream of money is stopped by a shortfall.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, famously drop the h at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Being open-eyed means being watchful and alert, fully conscious of what is happening.

clue.text: Roughly take down revolutionary leader

parts.note: ca, for circa, means roughly or approximately

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the word for take down is reversed

parts.note: to rase, or raze, a building is to take it down

explanation.surface: Bringing down a rebel leader, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar was the title of Roman emperors, and the word has come to mean an autocratic ruler.

clue.text: Not in show, dame discontented

parts.note: a demo is a demonstration or show

indicators.note: with its content, its middle, emptied out, only the outer letters of dame remain

explanation.surface: A dame, unhappy at not being in the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' looks like 'unhappy' but means emptied of contents.
explanation.definitionFit: Démodé is a French borrowing meaning out of fashion, so not in.

clue.text: Bust heaving very brazen

indicators.note: heaving means throwing out, so the letter for very is removed

parts.note: a business that has gone bust is insolvent

explanation.surface: A heaving bosom described as very shameless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' and 'heaving' suggest a bosom, but bust means bankrupt and heaving means throwing out.
explanation.definitionFit: An insolent person is boldly rude and shameless, which is what brazen describes.

clue.text: Plant hybrid more are using

indicators.note: a hybrid is a cross, so these letters are crossed into a new mix

explanation.surface: Gardeners are increasingly using a hybrid plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The rose geranium is a pelargonium grown for its rose-scented leaves, a garden plant.

clue.text: Men on board circling lake to find breeding-places

indicators.note: the chess pieces go round, or circle, the name of the lake

parts.note: rooks are chessmen, pieces on a board
Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: Sailors circling a lake on a boat look for nesting sites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men on board' suggests a crew on a ship; the board is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Rookeries are colonies where rooks, seabirds or seals breed and raise their young.

clue.text: Van is hell travelling round US city

indicators.note: letters travelling round move about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A van journey round an American city is miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Nashville is the capital of Tennessee and the home of country music.

clue.text: Shot home for some news

parts.note: a bullet is a shot fired from a gun
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A shot fired at a house makes the news.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short broadcast or printed report of the news.

clue.text: Note, after slaughter, reduced countries for final stages

indicators.note: after places the note following the cut-down slaughter word
reduced means the slaughter word loses its last letter

parts.note: a cull is the slaughter of selected animals
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
nations are countries

explanation.surface: A note about countries cutting back after a slaughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Culminations are the highest points or climaxes, the closing stages of a process.

clue.text: Minute drops in parent's drinks container

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for minute drops lower, further in the word for parent's

parts.note: mother's is the possessive of mother, a parent
mo is short for moment, a minute

explanation.surface: Minute traces are left in a parent's drinks flask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like 'tiny', but it is a short time, MO; it moves down from the front of MOTHERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thermos is a brand of vacuum flask for keeping drinks hot or cold.

clue.text: This writer disheartened orphan, the rotter

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the heart, so one middle letter goes

parts.note: Little Orphan Annie is the famous comic-strip and musical orphan

explanation.surface: The writer admits to upsetting an orphan, the rotter.
explanation.walkthrough: ANNIE is the orphan of the musical 'Annie'; losing its heart, one N, leaves ANIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A meanie is a nasty or ungenerous person, informally a rotter.

clue.text: Best lute I am playing with time inside

indicators.note: the letter for time is put inside the rearranged letters
playing a lute suggests the letters being played with, rearranged

explanation.surface: The best lute player is the one who keeps time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultimate as an adjective means the greatest or best possible.

clue.text: Very angry buccaneer heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter, the head, is removed

parts.note: a buccaneer is a pirate

explanation.surface: A furious buccaneer sets off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' looks like departing; it means losing the head letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate is a synonym for furious, meaning extremely angry.

clue.text: Top praise — People's Poet

indicators.note: to top is to cut the top off, here the first letter of each word

parts.note: to laud is to praise
men are people

explanation.surface: The highest praise goes to the people's poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like 'highest' but is a verb, beheading both LAUD and MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: W. H. Auden was a major Anglo-American poet of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Coveted object receives bid

indicators.note: the word for object receives, that is takes in, the word for bid

parts.note: an end is an object or aim
to vie is to bid or compete

explanation.surface: An object desired by others gets a bid at auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' looks like a thing, but it is an aim, END.
explanation.definitionFit: To have envied something is to have coveted it, wanting what another has.

clue.text: Fibre to remain rigid, having internal resistance

indicators.note: the word for remain rigid has the resistance letter inside it

parts.note: to stand is to stay upright and firm
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A fibre stays stiff because of its inner resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand is a single thread or filament, a fibre.

clue.text: Spooner's minor road excavation on major route

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words, as is done here

parts.note: a lane is a minor road
a mine is an excavation

explanation.surface: Digging work on a minor road along a major route.
explanation.definitionFit: A main line is a principal railway route or road.

clue.text: Popular plant, very big, for hostile locations

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a fern is a plant
OS stands for outsize, very big

explanation.surface: A popular, very large plant suited to tough places.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernos are blazing fires, places hellishly inhospitable to life.

clue.text: Kebab comes from this dirty place around end of block

indicators.note: the word for dirty place goes around the picked letter

parts.note: a sewer is a filthy place

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of block

explanation.surface: A kebab from a grubby place near the end of the street block.
explanation.definitionFit: A skewer is the spike on which a kebab is cooked and from which it is eaten.
